title: OAuth2/OIDC misconfiguration runner: detect redirect_uri bypass, PKCE absence, state parameter missing, and token leakage
goal: OAuth2/OIDC is the authentication backbone of modern applications. Misconfigurations lead to account takeover. This is not covered by any current runner. Implement an oauth-probe runner: (1) Discovery: detect OAuth2 endpoints by looking for /oauth/authorize, /oauth/token, /.well-known/openid-configuration, authorization_code patterns in JavaScript, and social login buttons. (2) redirect_uri bypass: test if the authorization server accepts: wildcard subdomains (https://evil.legitimate.com), path traversal (https://legit.com/../evil), open redirect chains as redirect URIs. Finding: 'OAuth2 Redirect URI Bypass — Account Takeover Possible'. (3) State parameter CSRF: check if the state parameter is present in authorization requests. If absent → OAuth CSRF (attacker can link their account to victim). (4) PKCE absent for SPAs: check if single-page app OAuth flows use PKCE (code_challenge). Absent PKCE in SPA → authorization code interception possible. (5) Token in URL: check if access tokens appear in URL fragments or redirect parameters (visible in browser history, referrer headers). (6) Token scope over-provisioning: request minimal scope, check if returned token grants broader access. (7) Implicit flow still supported: check if implicit flow (response_type=token) is enabled (deprecated, insecure). Active tier. Tool: custom Python using requests + browser automation.
scope: OAuth2/OIDC misconfigurations are in every major pentest standard (WSTG-SESS-10, OWASP Testing Guide). Not covered by any current runner. Critical for SaaS applications with 'Login with Google/Microsoft' or API-backed authentication.
generation_reason: OAuth2/OIDC testing absent from AegisPT — redirect_uri bypass, missing PKCE, token leakage are common real-world findings in modern SaaS applications.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Test only OAuth flows of the target application. Do not interact with third-party IdP endpoints (Google, Microsoft) directly.
